final_answer:
Let
\[
X=\frac U{\sqrt n},\qquad Y=\frac V{\sqrt n},
\]
where \(U,V\) are independent with density \(\pi^{-1/2}e^{-u^2}\). The given equation is exactly
\[
\mathbb P\left(V\ge \frac1n U^3e^{-U/\sqrt n}+\sqrt n\,\lambda_n\right)=\frac12.
\]
Write
\[
G(s)=\mathbb P(V\ge s)=\int_s^\infty \frac{e^{-v^2}}{\sqrt\pi}\,dv.
\]
Near \(0\),
\[
G(s)=\frac12-\frac{s}{\sqrt\pi}+O(s^3),
\]
since \(e^{-s^2}=1+O(s^2)\).

Put
\[
\sqrt n\,\lambda_n=a n^{-3/2}+b n^{-5/2}+o(n^{-5/2}).
\]
Then
\[
\frac1n U^3e^{-U/\sqrt n}
=
n^{-1}U^3-n^{-3/2}U^4+\frac12n^{-2}U^5-\frac16n^{-5/2}U^6+O(n^{-3}|U|^7)
\]
on the Gaussian main range, with tails exponentially negligible. Hence the threshold
\[
S_n=\frac1n U^3e^{-U/\sqrt n}+\sqrt n\,\lambda_n
\]
has expectation
\[
\mathbb E S_n
=
(a-\mathbb E U^4)n^{-3/2}
+\left(b-\frac16\mathbb E U^6\right)n^{-5/2}
+o(n^{-5/2}).
\]
For density \(\pi^{-1/2}e^{-u^2}\),
\[
\mathbb E U^4=\frac34,\qquad \mathbb E U^6=\frac{15}{8}.
\]
Also \(\mathbb E(S_n^3)=O(n^{-3})=o(n^{-5/2})\), so
\[
\mathbb E G(S_n)
=
\frac12-\frac1{\sqrt\pi}\mathbb E S_n+o(n^{-5/2}).
\]
The defining condition \(\mathbb E G(S_n)=1/2\) therefore forces
\[
a=\frac34,\qquad b=\frac16\cdot\frac{15}{8}=\frac{5}{16}.
\]
Thus
\[
\sqrt n\,\lambda_n=\frac{3}{4}n^{-3/2}+\frac{5}{16}n^{-5/2}+o(n^{-5/2}),
\]
so
\[
\lambda_n=\frac{3}{4n^2}+\frac{5}{16n^3}+o(n^{-3}).
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac{5}{16}}.
\]
